body:
All our other "chained" constraints produce a single result because that's what the Assert methods expect to deal with. Internally, they look at the nested constraint in producing their result. It seems like this was missed in `PropertyConstraint`. 

IMO, a linked chain of constraint results gives Assert too much to do. Note that whatever Assert needs to do, Assume, Warn and any other similar classes also have to do. Having a single `ConstraintResult` was intended to simplify things for those upstream classes. The idea was that `ConstraintResult` should be the class that knows how to "flatten" the chain or tree of nested `Constraints`.

@CharliePoole I don't understand how this impacts `Assert` and the rest. They still get handed a single `ConstraintResult`. They don't know that it is a `ChainedConstraintResult`, and even if they did, they can't access the chain.

The chain is retained as a private implementation detail because otherwise the logic for writing the message is not retained.

See my edit of the first comment.

`Assert` etc. need a "flattened" result. `ConstraintResult` or it's derivative is supposed to provide it. `ConstraintResult` already has access to a chain of `Constraints` to allow it to produce that result. Creating a chain of `ConstraintResults` seems like an unnecessary level of complexity to me, unless there is something we can do with a chain of results that we can't do with a chain of constraints.

Taking this further, would you implement a chain of results for every constraint that uses a base constraint? For binary constraints? I'm for it if it enables some feature we want to implement, although even then I'd prefer to just fix the bug before coming back and rewriting all constraints.
@CharliePoole I guess I'm just not seeing a simpler way to flatten the results than the one I proposed. But I'm now very interested to see one. 😃

`AndConstraint` does the [exact same thing](https://github.com/nunit/nunit/blob/master/src/NUnitFramework/framework/Constraints/AndConstraint.cs#L73) I'm proposing for `PropertyConstraint`!

Hmm, I see that I need to make a correction though. I should only be delegating `WriteActualValueTo` to the base constraint, not `WriteMessage`, or otherwise the property's prefix on the message would never be shown. Nor would anything higher up.

 Then if I make `ChainedConstraintResult` nested and private and name it `PropertyConstraintResult` on the assumption that it won't see any reuse either directly or as a base class, then I’ve exactly duplicated your technique with the binary operators.

But maybe that was your point all along?
Maybe I misunderstood. Don't we already have `PropertyConstraintResult`?

I did misunderstand...

Currently we have chained constraints but only one result is produced for the chain.

My understanding was that you would create a mesh like this...
```
ConstraintResult ==> NestedResult1     ==> NestedResult2     ==> etc.
     |                     |                     |
     V                     V                     V
Constraint       ==> NestedConstraint1 ==> NestedConstraint2 ==> etc.
```

I'm totally in favor of doing it like AndConstraint. See also EqualConstraint.

Ah, okay. We do not have a `PropertyConstraintResult`.

So what do you think of keeping it as an internal `ChainedConstraintResult` class to be directly used or extended for use in constraints with exactly one base constraint? Meh?

Personally I like a nested class that is tailored for exactly the constraint in which it is nested. If you create a reusable class, then you're almost certain to run into cases where it needs to test what it's being used for and do something different. Either way the code is minimal though, so it can be changed later if that happens.

### Notes to implementors

All we need is the class defined above and to use `return new PropertyConstraintResult(this, baseResult);` instead of this line:

https://github.com/nunit/nunit/blob/bf8f2dc863036655dc37583dd5b7408b356b6026/src/NUnitFramework/framework/Constraints/PropertyConstraint.cs#L74

And we need a test that fails before and succeeds afterwards, confirming that `PropertyConstraint.ApplyTo(...).WriteActualValueTo` calls the base constraint's result's `WriteActualValueTo`.

I'm surprised you aren't doing it, since you wrote the code already. 😄 

Doesn't your `PropertyConstraintResult` code simply give the message of the base constraint, rather than any thing like "Expected property Name equal to "xxxx" but was ÿyyy"?

I most likely am doing it, but why discourage someone else from saving me the hassle? 😁
Plus, good tests are more work than implementation. Plus, I like inviting collaboration.

No, I fixed that by removing the `WriteMessage` override earlier. It keeps the message but swaps out the writing of the “actual value” part of the message. Before, we were simply writing the actual value object in that place. Now we are calling the base result's actual value writer instead, which itself may only write the actual value by default.
I'll help out with this one. Been looking for a project I actually use to help out with and what better time than Hacktoberfest. 😃
Awesome! It's yours. 😃 @rprouse can you invite and assign?
@Steve-Boyd I've sent an invite to the contributors team which allows us to assign issues to you. One of the team will assign this issue once you accept, just ping us here.
